text:
Priya: Heads-up: seeing slow sustained memory growth when running streaming chat interleaved with tool loops on ded. node. ~15% RSS over 90m on synthetic run.
Omar: Which workload exactly? single session or many?
Priya: Single long session, pattern: stream ~4k tokens, call tool A, resume stream, repeat. Repro harness attached in the PR.
Linh: Any allocation hotspots from pprof?
Priya: Quick heap diff (pprof top):
```
heap profile: 68.4MB total
  28.1MB  kv_prefix::Shard (n=512)
  12.6MB  allocator.slab_pages (n=96)
   9.3MB  prefix_index::Node (n=1024)
   6.5MB  small_objs
   4.0MB  runtime.gc_stacks
```
Casey: Looks like prefix shards keep residency. Do you see pin/hold counts on the shards?
Priya: yes — grep of internal counters shows many shards with hold_count > 0 long after tool returns. Example line: `shard[0x1f3].hold=2 last_touch=2026-04-23T11:02:05Z` while session continued.
Omar: Could be eviction policy hysteresis: we bump hold on streaming append to avoid evicting active prefixes; tool calls reuse prefixes but maybe never trigger eviction because session stays "active" due to the stream being paused/awaiting tool.
Linh: Another angle: kernel selection for large-token streams prefers big-page allocation path, which reduces fragmentation but also pins pages differently. Any change in mmapping or madvise recently?
Priya: We didn't change madvise. But I did notice an earlier commit that added a per-shard pin during tool-call to avoid tearing; comment says `// pin until tool finishes` but no symmetric release in the tool-return path.
Casey: That sounds like a bug. Are there races that could prevent release? If release is deferred to a GC cycle it's possible long sessions accumulate many pins.
Priya: Repro experiment: enabled aggressive eviction flags `--kv-evict-mode=aggressive --kv-evict-min-keep=5` and ran 60m. Memory stopped increasing but p95 token latency doubled (110ms -> 220ms).
Omar: Tradeoff confirmed. Can't globally force eviction in prod. Need targeted release semantics when a tool returns.
Linh: Proposed fix: add explicit `unpin_on_tool_return(session_id)` call path that releases stale prefix shards asynchronously and bounded. Important: don't release shards that were appended to in the last N seconds.
Priya: Sketch:
```
// on tool return
func onToolReturn(sid string) {
  go func() {
    time.Sleep(150 * time.Millisecond)
    if now.Sub(sessionLastAppend(sid)) > 3 * time.Second {
      released := prefixCache.ReleaseStaleForSession(sid, keepRecent=8, maxWork=64)
      metrics.Counter("kv.prefix.released").Add(float64(released))
    }
  }()
}
```
Casey: Need to guard against concurrent append racing with the release. Use an atomic last_append_ts and check it before releasing each shard. Better: include a per-session CAS token that increments on append; pass the token to release call and only release shards if token unchanged.
Omar: Also add a circuit to avoid repeated churn: don't run release more than once per X seconds per session, and backoff if release_count high.
Priya: I'll implement CAS token + backoff + metrics. Also will add a histogram `kv.prefix.keep_age_seconds` and `kv.prefix.release_batch_size`.
Linh: Add a small microbench for the eviction path: toggle on/off and measure CPU per token, and p95 impact. We need numbers before merging.
Casey: Also add a smoke test that simulates: 1 session streaming 4k tokens, tool loop x10 with brief tool returns, assert RSS delta < 5% over 30m.
Priya: Ran a quick dev branch with async release + CAS token. 3h run shows flat memory (variance <3%). Release batches average 12 shards. p95 increased ~8ms.
infra-bot: Incident created: IR-2026-0424 (mem_growth_stream_toolloop). Owner: Priya.
Omar: Sounds good. One nit: ensure ReleaseStaleForSession respects shard pin semantics for shared shards across sessions (don't double free). Use refcount decrement, not free.
Priya: Yes reworked to call `shard.DecRef()` and rely on existing free path. Added unit tests for refcount flow.
Linh: Nice. After bench numbers and SRE review, we can roll to canary and monitor `kv.prefix.memory_bytes` and `kv.prefix.release_ops_total`.
Casey: Let's also add an alert: if prefix_release_rate > X and p95 latency regression > Y then auto-disable the feature. Safer rollout.
Priya: Adding alert + rollout plan in PR description. Putting up PR now with tests and metrics.
Omar: Thanks team. Good catch — policy+missing-release rather than allocator leak. :thumbsup:
